tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.does: General AI assistant: chat, writing, analysis, images, voice, web search and agents.
pros: Large ecosystem of GPTs and integrations
cons: Best features need a paid plan

tools.name: Claude
tools.does: AI assistant strong at writing, analysis, long documents and coding.
cons: Fewer built-in media tools than some rivals

tools.name: Gemini
tools.does: Google's AI assistant, connected to Search, Gmail, Docs and YouTube.
cons: Integration value depends on using Google apps

tools.name: Microsoft Copilot
tools.does: AI assistant in Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft apps.
cons: Office integration needs a Microsoft 365 plan
Several Copilot brands can be confusing

tools.name: Grok
tools.does: AI assistant integrated with X (Twitter), with real-time post search.
cons: Closely tied to the X platform

tools.name: Meta AI
tools.does: AI assistant inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger, built on Llama.
pros: Free and inside apps people already use

tools.name: DeepSeek
tools.does: Chat app and low-cost API for DeepSeek's open-weight reasoning models.
cons: Data stored in China may not suit some organizations

tools.name: Le Chat
tools.does: Mistral's assistant with web search, documents and code.

tools.name: Perplexity
tools.does: AI answer engine that searches the web and cites its sources.
cons: Quality depends on the sources it finds
Advanced modes need a paid plan

tools.name: Kimi
tools.does: AI assistant known for long-context reading and open-weight models.

tools.name: Qwen Chat
tools.does: Chat app for Alibaba's Qwen models, many of them open-weight.
cons: Smaller app ecosystem in the West

tools.name: NotebookLM
tools.does: Research notebook that answers only from the documents you upload, and makes audio overviews.
pros: Answers grounded in your own sources
cons: Limited to the sources you add

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.does: Agentic coding tool in the terminal and IDEs: reads code, edits files, runs commands and tests.
pros: Handles multi-step tasks end to end
Extensible with skills, plugins and MCP
cons: Usage costs can grow on big tasks

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.does: AI pair programmer in VS Code, JetBrains and GitHub: completions, chat and coding agent.
pros: Works in the most popular editors

tools.name: Cursor
tools.does: AI-first code editor (VS Code-based) with chat, multi-file edits and agents.

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.does: Coding agent in the terminal (open-source CLI), IDE and cloud.
tools.cost: Included with ChatGPT plans or API
pros: Can run tasks in the cloud
cons: Best experience needs a paid plan

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.does: Open-source AI agent for the terminal, powered by Gemini.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.does: AI code editor with an agent that plans and edits across files.

tools.name: Aider
tools.does: AI pair programming in the terminal that edits files and commits to git.
pros: Open source, works with many models
cons: You pay for the model API

tools.name: Replit Agent
tools.does: Builds and deploys full apps in the browser from a prompt.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.does: Creates web apps from chat, with a database and deployment.

tools.name: v0
tools.does: Generates React and Next.js user interfaces and apps from prompts.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.does: Builds, runs and deploys full-stack web apps in the browser from prompts.
cons: Larger projects get harder to manage

tools.name: Midjourney
tools.does: Generates artistic, high-quality images from text prompts.
cons: Less precise with text in images

tools.name: GPT Image (in ChatGPT)
tools.does: Creates and edits images by chatting in ChatGPT or through the API.

tools.name: Stable Diffusion
tools.does: Open image-generation models you can run locally or in apps.
tools.cost: Open models; paid API/licenses for some uses

tools.name: Adobe Firefly
tools.does: Image and design generation built into Photoshop, Illustrator and Express.
pros: Inside Adobe tools designers already use

tools.name: FLUX
tools.does: Image-generation models, some open-weight, known for realism and prompt accuracy.

tools.name: Ideogram
tools.does: Image generator known for accurate text inside images (logos, posters).

tools.name: Canva AI
tools.does: AI design tools in Canva: images, writing, presentations and editing.
pros: Templates plus AI in one place
cons: Best AI features on paid plans
Less control than pro design tools

tools.name: Sora
tools.does: Generates video clips from text and images.

tools.name: Veo
tools.does: Google's video-generation model, available in Gemini, Flow and Vertex AI.

tools.name: Runway
tools.does: AI video generation and editing tools for creators.
pros: Many video tools in one place

tools.name: Kling
tools.does: Text- and image-to-video generation.

tools.name: Synthesia
tools.does: Creates presenter videos with AI avatars for training and communications.

tools.name: HeyGen
tools.does: AI avatar videos and video translation with lip-sync.

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.does: Realistic text-to-speech, voice cloning and dubbing.

tools.name: Suno
tools.does: Generates songs with vocals from a text prompt.
cons: Commercial use needs a paid plan

tools.name: Whisper
tools.does: Open-source speech-to-text model for transcription and translation.
cons: No live meeting features by itself

tools.name: Otter.ai
tools.does: Transcribes and summarizes meetings in Zoom, Teams and Google Meet.

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.does: AI meeting assistant: records, transcribes and summarizes calls.
cons: Bot joining calls can bother attendees

tools.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
tools.does: AI inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, grounded in your work data.
pros: Works across your Office files and mail
cons: Value depends on how well data is organized

tools.name: Gemini for Google Workspace
tools.does: Gemini inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides and Meet.

tools.name: Notion AI
tools.does: AI writing, search and Q&A across your Notion workspace.
pros: Searches all your notes and docs
Good for teams already on Notion
cons: Only as useful as your Notion content

tools.name: Grammarly
tools.does: AI writing assistant for grammar, tone and rewriting everywhere you type.
pros: Works in most apps and browsers

tools.name: Gamma
tools.does: Creates presentations, documents and web pages from a prompt.

tools.name: Hugging Face
tools.does: Hub for open models, datasets and demo apps (Spaces), plus the Transformers library.

tools.name: LangChain
tools.does: Framework for building LLM apps and agents (chains, tools, RAG); LangGraph for agent workflows.

tools.name: LlamaIndex
tools.does: Framework for connecting LLMs to your data: ingestion, indexing and RAG.

tools.name: Ollama
tools.does: Runs open models (Llama, Qwen, Gemma and more) on your own computer with one command.
cons: Needs a capable GPU or Mac for big models
Slower than cloud for large models

tools.name: LM Studio
tools.does: Desktop app to download, chat with and serve local models.

tools.name: vLLM
tools.does: High-throughput engine for serving LLMs (PagedAttention, continuous batching).

tools.name: NVIDIA NIM
tools.does: Prebuilt, optimized containers for running AI models on NVIDIA GPUs.
tools.cost: Free to try; NVIDIA AI Enterprise license for production

tools.name: PyTorch
tools.does: The most widely used deep-learning framework for research and production.

tools.name: TensorFlow
tools.does: Deep-learning framework with strong production and mobile tooling.
cons: Less popular than PyTorch for new research

tools.name: Weights & Biases
tools.does: Experiment tracking, model evaluation and LLM observability.

tools.name: Pinecone
tools.does: Managed vector database for semantic search and RAG.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.does: Open-source embedding database, easy to start with for RAG.
cons: Fewer enterprise features than managed options

tools.name: n8n
tools.does: Workflow automation with AI agent nodes; self-hostable.
cons: Complex flows get hard to maintain

tools.name: Zapier
tools.does: No-code automation across thousands of apps, with AI steps and agents.

tools.name: Amazon Bedrock
tools.does: Managed access to many foundation models (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Amazon Nova) with agents and RAG.

tools.name: Azure AI Foundry
tools.does: Build, evaluate and deploy AI apps and agents with OpenAI and other models on Azure.

tools.name: Google Vertex AI
tools.does: Google Cloud platform for Gemini and other models, training, tuning and MLOps.
pros: Full ML lifecycle in one place

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.does: One API to access hundreds of models from many providers.
cons: Extra hop between you and the provider

tools.name: Groq
tools.does: Very fast inference for open models on custom LPU chips, via API.

tools.name: MCP (Model Context Protocol)
tools.does: Open protocol for connecting AI apps to tools and data sources.
pros: Write a tool once, use it in many AI apps
cons: Security of third-party servers must be checked
